title: The Goodman-Carter integrated European band that never happened
summary: Hammond and Goodman planned a hyphenated-leadership all-star integrated band in 1934; it never took place.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Right. Of course, in jazz history, there's a lot of things like that - and to put in a plug for Oral History, that's why it's very important to do this kind of thing because things are announced in music journals and they don't always take place.
Right.
And people read the announcement, and assume that something actually happened, which never did happen.
Right.
And there are lots of things like that. I remember. And while we're on that, let's skip

ahead a minute and ask about the -- a case like that I think I remember in which John Hammond and Benny Goodman and sometime in late 1934, if I remember correctly, were planning to put together a tremendous all star band to bring -- to tour Europe.
Yeah, an integrated band.
Right, an integrated band. And you were to play alto with that group.
Well, it was to have been in hyphenated leadership.
Ah, with Benny Goodman.
Benny Goodman and Benny Carter, yeah. That was John's idea at the moment.
Yeah. And I think Billy was supposed to be on that tour.
Billy Holiday?
Yeah, that was not part of it.
At that time ... that was a little early. Or it might have been, I'm not sure.
Or maybe it was Ella.
No, not Ella.
No, it couldn't have been Ella.
Not at that time, no.
Right. And that didn't take place, either?
No, it didn't.
That sounds like a ...
That's right.
I think it was called the Dream Orchestra or something, or ...
It could have been. I ...
People were referring to it as a dream band or something like that.
